degradeDesign.problem: QA now captures properties no SiteSpec style token contains. diffStyles compares spec-expected vs captured, so those properties have nothing to compare against.
degradeDesign.behaviour: diffStyles is UNCHANGED and iterates the spec's own property keys, so an extra captured property is never compared, never crashes it and never manufactures a mismatch (asserted).
degradeDesign.honesty: Silence is not equality, so two mechanisms name the gap instead: (1) unverifiableFromSpecProperties(specVocabulary) returns the sorted QA properties the spec cannot adjudicate, so a report can say un-verifiable-from-spec rather than imply equal; (2) compareCapturedStyles(original, clone) compares two LIVE captures browser-to-browser — that axis needs no observer data at all, so the QA-only tail is fully verifiable there. The mandated fixture exercises exactly that path.
degradeDesign.consumersChecked: style-diff.ts (spec-driven, safe), classify-diff.ts / propose-corrections.ts / emit-diffs.ts read style mismatch records only; nothing in the repo assumed QA properties are a subset of the observer's.

risks: The QA list is a literal snapshot of STYLE_WHITELIST (114 properties) as of this change. If the observer builder adds further properties after this, the suite's 'QA keeps every property the Observer records' check will fail until the new property is copied into QA_STYLE_PROPERTIES. That failure is the intended alarm, not a bug — but it is a real coupling in maintenance, and the fix is a one-line literal addition.

Capture cost: 30 extra getPropertyValue calls per element per capture, and most of them (direction, fill, outline-*, text-indent, word-spacing…) return a value on every element, so each captured element's style map grows by roughly a quarter. Raw captures are in-memory only (not persisted), but a very large page's QA run now holds more. Not measured on a real site here.

ΔE76 adds ~6 cbrt + 2 matrix multiplies per DIFFERING pixel (identical pixels are short-circuited to 0, and sRGB→linear is a 256-entry LUT). On a page where the @1 ratio really is ~1.0 — exactly the 28.5A case — that short-circuit does not fire and a full-page pair gets measurably slower. No timing was taken on a real full-page screenshot; worth watching on the first real run.

compareCapturedStyles matches elements by capture key. Original-mode keys are document-order indices, so it is only meaningful between two captures of the same DOM shape (the fixture's case, and original-vs-clone where the clone walk emits SiteSpec node ids). It reports unmatchedKeys / tagMismatchKeys rather than guessing when the shapes differ; it is NOT a general alignment algorithm and should not be used as one.

src/cli-qa-reconstruction.ts still prints only the @1 median (lines 153 and 173) — outside this builder's ownership. The new medians are in the summary object and in worstPages detail, but the CLI's headline still shows one scalar until someone extends it.

The curated 30 are a judgement call about what paints. Properties deliberately left out include caret-color (pointless per brief), will-change, perspective, backface-visibility, shape-outside, text-emphasis and the border-image longhands beyond border-image-source.
